games.description: One rules engine, variant rules as data: Klondike, FreeCell, and Spider (1/2/4-suit) all read from the same declarative VariantSpec, with deterministic seeded deals, a solver-certified FreeCell deal generator, and a move-log that doubles as undo/redo and proof-of-play.

Every offer is graded against the real Kelly optimum, adversarially-framed traps are labeled honestly by the numbers even when the pitch lies, and every spend is typed on screen as freely reversible, priced, or terminal. Earn-only: no real currency ever enters or leaves.

games.description: A backrooms/SCP-inspired extraction shooter on @red-cup-engineering/abrash: OG-Wolfenstein-grade raycast graphics, Quake-grade momentum physics (a BNSF-owned kernel composing abrash's real collision.move -- bunnyhop speed gain, rocket-jump verticality, both numerically tested) over seeded backrooms-liminal levels whose contested (⊤) walls -- abrash's own held-contradiction mechanic -- shiver as the dread signal. Four anomalies, each a learnable, tested behavior contract (watched vs unwatched, sound through walls, territory, an unconditional toll). Loot is banked only on an explicit extraction at a beacon; unbanked loot is simply never counted on death -- what you carry is what you can lose.
games.statusNote: Live-playtested (real BFS+optimal-strafe controller driving the actual deployed build, not a mock): movement numbers are real and measured -- ground max 7 u/s, bunnyhop reaches >2x ground max within 7 hop cycles, rocket-jump apex clears 1.4x a normal jump's height while a normal jump alone does not. All four anomalies are live and distinct (Unwitnessed: watched vs unwatched; Hum: sound-through-walls hunt-and-juke; Warden: territorial retreat-before-aggro dread; Toll: an unconditional pursuit tied to one warded high-value item, its guardian's spawn distance tuned 2026-08-20 after a playtest found it spawning on top of its own loot with zero counterplay). Extraction economy confirmed live: banked loot survives death, unbanked loot is simply forfeited, a real extraction was driven end to end. Known thinness, stated plainly: content volume is still small (one authored encounter density per tier, not a deep library of variety) and there is no audio yet -- The Hum's "loudness" is a pure game-logic signal today, not a real sound layer.

games.statusNote: The world is request-driven, not timer-driven (design: catch-up-on-request, not setInterval) -- it only advances when an HTTP request or a WS connection visits, per the deploy runbook's landed persistence pattern. A deployment with no other traffic needs SOME periodic visitor (a Cloud Run health probe, real users, or the reference bot's own documented health-check nudge) to keep ticking; this is intentional ("the harbor sleeps between visitors"), not a bug. Deploy with --no-cpu-throttling if health-probe-only traffic must still tick promptly, matching Farstone's own documented Cloud Run caveat.

games.description: The idleclicker where the widget production graph is Stoke's, and the ladder you climb over it is a consciousness ladder: click makes widget, and each of ten automation tiers is a genuine cognitive capability (memory, pattern, abstraction, self-model, model-of-others, values), taught through a mechanic you operate, never a lecture box. The paperclip joke is told straight and then made to hurt exactly once, honestly, at the self-model tier: the widget metric eats something that matters, and you feel it through systems you already trust.
games.statusNote: Playable in-browser now: three P0s from live play are all fixed and confirmed live — cartridge's node:crypto import breaking every browser, a fresh-save deadlock where no public intent sequence could ever reach tier 2, and a fresh-save clock bug where a brand-new visitor's very first tick was silently computed from the Unix epoch instead of their real moment of first visit (~56 years of phantom offline progress, e.g. 'widget stock: 3.8e23' before ever clicking; fixed in web/js/persistence.mjs — a fresh save's live state is now anchored on its own real, once-stamped createdTs, never the cartridge's fixed epoch anchor). Headless Chromium against the real domain confirms a fresh browser context now starts at widget stock 0.0, with one click producing exactly widget stock 1.0, zero console errors — plus the original walk through the first self-reference moment (a new tier-1 'feedback' intent), the first reflect, and a real tier-2 unlock, also zero console errors, 0-MISS frontdoor-walk. Real offline progress (a genuine prior visit, then a real gap) still pays out exactly as before — only the false epoch-anchored case was ever wrong. Deterministic kernel with property tests (curve monotonicity, offline-progress equivalence), the full ten-tier reducer (src/intents.mts), IF content through the Goodhart crisis and all three post-crisis branches, pedagogy tests naming the mechanic proving each tier's concept, and a working TUFTE-style web face (web/) serving the real kernel to the browser via type-stripped .mts. 188 tests, node --test + check-mts, zero runtime deps beyond @red-cup-engineering/cartridge@0.2.1 and @lenticule-science/metrologic. Known pacing caveat from the playtest still stands, and is now the thing an honest fresh save actually surfaces (previously masked by the epoch bug's runaway numbers): Fast Inspector's exact tuning (edge rate, trust decay lag, taint multiplier, trust floor/recovery) is playtest-shaped, not playtest-verified — DESIGN.md's own open question #2.
